subject: Recap + next steps: HIPAA scope and deployment paths for Galaxy Health
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Brooks <samantha.brooks@galaxyhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: HIPAA scope and deployment paths for Galaxy Health

Hi Samantha — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Call highlights
- SOC 2: Redwood currently maintains SOC 2 Type I (control design) and is in progress toward a Type II attestation. I listed expected timelines below.
- BAA: We can sign a BAA for PHI use cases. Need to confirm which deployment model you prefer (see options).
- PHI scope: You mentioned patient identifiers, MRNs, and clinical notes/transcripts. Confirming whether identifiers + clinical text will be stored vs. processed in-memory only will affect recommended hosting.

Deployment options (high level)
- Hosted API (Redwood-managed): fastest onboarding and cost-effective but NOT eligible for PHI under standard offering.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): tenant-isolated GPU pools; eligible for PHI with a signed BAA and agreed network controls (recommended for most SaaS health workloads).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-controlled network and key management; recommended if your procurement or regulator requires customer-managed infrastructure or air-gapping.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Please confirm exact PHI types and whether you need at-rest storage of PHI or only in-memory processing.
2) Please fill and return the vendor security questionnaire attached (or send your security team's DOCX).
3) If you prefer a technical deep-dive on Dedicated vs Private (network, keys, logs), we can schedule a 60-90 minute session next week.

Attached: redwood-baa-summary-2027-10.pdf (summary of BAA terms), redwood-hosting-matrix.xlsx (feature/controls comparison).

We’ll loop in Aditya (solutions lead) once we have the PHI confirmation so he can prepare a network/ops sketch.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Samantha Brooks <samantha.brooks@galaxyhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Galaxy Health Security Team <security@galaxyhealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-11T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: HIPAA scope and deployment paths for Galaxy Health

Hi Irene — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

PHI scope
- Types: patient name, MRN, DOB, encounter metadata, and clinical notes (transcribed from provider calls). We do not intend to store PHI long-term on vendor side beyond what’s needed for session processing unless explicitly agreed.

SOC 2 / procurement timeline
- Our security team needs a SOC 2 Type II report and a signed BAA before we can go to procurement. If Redwood’s Type II is not available, we need an interim plan (e.g., Dedicated with compensating controls). Can you confirm Redwood’s current state and expected Type II date?

Questionnaire
- Attached is our vendor security questionnaire (vendor_security_questionnaire_galaxy_2027.docx). Please have the security/ops team complete and return.

Forwarding to our procurement lead for timeline visibility. Also, can you provide a short summary (1 page) of what Dedicated includes from a network/logging/retention perspective?

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Brooks
Head of Integrations | Galaxy Health
samantha.brooks@galaxyhealth.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Brooks <samantha.brooks@galaxyhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-13T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: HIPAA scope and deployment paths for Galaxy Health

Thanks Samantha — answers inline below and a suggested path forward.

On 2027-10-11 09:04, Samantha Brooks wrote:
> PHI scope
> - Types: patient name, MRN, DOB, encounter metadata, and clinical notes (transcribed from provider calls). We do not intend to store PHI long-term on vendor side beyond what’s needed for session processing unless explicitly agreed.

Understood — that exact scope maps cleanly to two common recommendations: (A) if you strictly require no at-rest PHI on vendor side, we recommend Private VPC or on-prem; (B) if short-term ephemeral storage is acceptable with strict retention (e.g., <24 hours) and auditability, Dedicated with configured retention policies and KV/prefix caching disabled for sensitive routes is commonly used. We can include explicit retention clauses in the BAA appendix.

> SOC 2 / procurement timeline
> - Our security team needs a SOC 2 Type II report and a signed BAA before we can go to procurement. If Redwood’s Type II is not available, we need an interim plan (e.g., Dedicated with compensating controls). Can you confirm Redwood’s current state and expected Type II date?

Redwood status: we currently hold SOC 2 Type I (control design). Our Type II engagement is in flight — expected targeting completion and public attestation by 2028-01 (Q1 2028). For customers with near-term deadlines, we offer Dedicated + contractual compensating controls (network allowlists, customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM, extended logging retention to your SIEM) and can provide our control evidence pack progressively. Aditya, can you confirm typical compensating-control set we offer for Dedicated PHI customers?

> Questionnaire
> - Attached is our vendor security questionnaire (vendor_security_questionnaire_galaxy_2027.docx). Please have the security/ops team complete and return.

Will do — forwarding this to our security ops and compliance team for completion. Expect first-pass answers within 3 business days. We’ll attach evidence where available and flag items requiring follow-up.

Suggested next steps (proposal)
1) Redwood to return completed questionnaire + preliminary evidence (network/topology, controls matrix) — target 2027-10-17.
2) Technical deep-dive on Dedicated vs Private (ops + security) — propose Tue 2027-10-19 10:00-11:30 PT. Please confirm availability.
3) If you confirm Dedicated is acceptable, we’ll draft a BAA appendix covering retention, access controls, incident response SLAs, and an explicit no-long-term-storage clause unless mutually agreed.

Attachments to follow: network-arch-draft.png (ops sketch) and an annotated BAA summary.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
